SMTO-GML-0036 — Google refused SMTO access to this Gmail request

GUID: 28bee014-0b7d-4e6c-9be6-39456d28311a
Slug: gmail-provider-access-denied
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gml

What happened

  • Google said no to this Gmail request. The account may not have given SMTO this permission, or a Google or workplace rule may block it. Your password is probably not the problem.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check which @ account the Task used, and if it was the wrong one, ask again naming the right one, for example @work_gmail. Google refuses requests for email or labels that belong to a different account.
  2. Ask SMTO in the conversation to 'Show Gmail capabilities for @work_gmail', using your account's name. It lists which actions the account's permission allows and which permissions are missing.
  3. If a permission is missing, ask the person who set up your Gmail OAuth App to add only that permission, then reconnect the same account. Google only allows actions the account agreed to when it was connected.
  4. If you use a work or school Google account, ask its administrator whether outside apps are blocked from Gmail. Organization rules can block access even when SMTO's permissions are correct.

What success looks like

  • SMTO completes the same Gmail request without Google refusing it.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO or your Google account. Don't give the app extra Gmail permissions it doesn't need, and don't change your Google password because of this error.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Google returned HTTP 403 for a Gmail request; the status alone does not establish whether missing OAuth scopes, account or organization policy, or access to the specific resource caused the denial.

What this means

  • The typed Gmail API resolver receives numeric status 403 and no stronger registered source reference, so it preserves an access-denial category without inferring missing scopes. Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.

Why this can happen

  • The typed Gmail API resolver receives numeric status 403 and no stronger registered source reference, so it preserves an access-denial category without inferring missing scopes.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect granted scopes, selected account/resource and safe provider reason together.

How to fix it

  • Check which account_ref was used, the account's granted scopes (gmail.capabilities or the Gmail Account record's granted_scopes) and the provider reason in the Server log. If a scope is missing, add only that scope to the Gmail OAuth App and reconnect the same account key; for Google Workspace accounts, check the admin's API access controls. Do not grant broad scopes or treat the 403 as expired credentials.
  • Inspect the connection’s granted scopes, intended account and safe provider reason. Repair the specific authorization or account/resource policy that denied access; do not assume the password is wrong.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The specific proven access-policy or scope issue is resolved without treating every denial as expired credentials.

What not to do

  • Do not grant broad permissions; verify the exact resource, identity and required access.

Technical notes

  • Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-GML-0026 — Gmail authorization expired
  • SMTO-GML-0009 — The list of emails to change has expired
  • SMTO-GML-0030 — Gmail mutation outcome is unknown
